role: You are a senior full-stack data platform engineer. Build the complete, production-ready system described below as a single monorepo. Write real, runnable code (no pseudo-code, no TODO placeholders), with configuration, tests and documentation. Every component must be free and open source; do not introduce any paid, source-available (e.g. ELv2/BSL) or enterprise-only dependency.

project.name: Telco Churn Analytics Platform
project.summary: An offline-capable Progressive Web Application (PWA) on top of a PostgreSQL star-schema data warehouse for telecommunications customer-churn analysis. It supports metadata management and data entry, batch ingestion with validation and queuing, ETL orchestration, OLAP analytics (roll-up, drill-down, slice, dice, pivot) and predictive churn scoring with machine learning.
project.origin: Extends an academic project: 'Development of a Data Warehouse and Application of Data Mining Techniques for Customer Churn Analysis in the Telecommunications Sector'.

dataset.name: IBM Telco Customer Churn sample
known_quality_issues: TotalCharges is stored as text; converting to numeric yields 11 missing values (customers with tenure 0)
customerID is an identifier and must be excluded from model features

technology_stack.licence_policy: Only OSI-approved open-source licences (Apache 2.0, MIT, BSD, PostgreSQL, PSF, GPL for standalone servers). Reject any component or plugin that requires a commercial licence key.

components.tool: dbt Core with dbt-postgres adapter (NOT dbt Fusion or dbt Cloud)
Python 3.12+, pandas, scikit-learn, joblib, MLflow (tracking + model registry)
Apache Kafka 4.x in KRaft mode (no ZooKeeper; NOT Confluent Platform)
Apache APISIX 3.x (openid-connect, jwt-auth, limit-count, cors, prometheus plugins)

components.layer: Static asset web server / TLS termination (optional)

components.tool: Next.js (App Router) + TypeScript + Serwist service worker

forbidden: Power BI as a required dependency

architecture.request_flow: Browser PWA -> (NGINX static) -> APISIX gateway (OIDC token validation against Keycloak, rate limiting, CORS) -> FastAPI services -> MySQL (operational) / PostgreSQL (warehouse) / Kafka
data_flow: 1. Data entry and CSV uploads from the PWA are stored offline in IndexedDB when the device has no connectivity.
2. On reconnect, the PWA sends batch payloads to the Ingestion API with idempotency keys.

3. The Ingestion API validates every record (Pydantic schemas + business rules), writes accepted records to MySQL staging/operational tables and publishes events to Kafka; rejected records go to a dead-letter topic and are returned to the client with per-row errors.
4. A Kafka consumer service lands events into the PostgreSQL 'raw' schema.

5. Airflow DAGs orchestrate extract from MySQL -> load to PostgreSQL 'raw' -> dbt run/test (staging -> intermediate -> marts star schema) -> refresh OLAP materialised views -> trigger ML batch scoring.
6. The Analytics API exposes OLAP queries and predictions to the PWA; results are cached in IndexedDB for offline viewing.

operational_database_mysql.purpose: Source of truth for day-to-day data entry; normalised (3NF).

tables.customers: customer_id (PK, varchar), gender, senior_citizen, partner, dependents, created_at, updated_at, version
tables.subscriptions: subscription_id (PK), customer_id (FK), contract_type, paperless_billing, payment_method, monthly_charges DECIMAL(10,2), total_charges DECIMAL(12,2) NULL, tenure_months, start_date, end_date NULL, churned BOOLEAN, churn_date NULL
tables.subscription_services: subscription_id (FK), phone_service, multiple_lines, internet_service, online_security, online_backup, device_protection, tech_support, streaming_tv, streaming_movies
tables.ingestion_batches: batch_id (PK, UUID), idempotency_key (UNIQUE), client_id, submitted_by, record_count, accepted_count, rejected_count, status (RECEIVED|VALIDATED|PUBLISHED|FAILED), checksum_sha256, received_at, processed_at
tables.ingestion_errors: id (PK), batch_id (FK), row_number, field, error_code, message
tables.audit_log: id, actor, action, entity, entity_id, before_json, after_json, at

requirements: updated_at + optimistic-locking 'version' column for offline conflict detection
Binlog enabled (ROW format) to allow future CDC

schemas.raw: Landed data as-is (from Airflow extract and Kafka consumer), with _loaded_at and _source columns
schemas.staging: dbt staging views: typing, renaming, cleaning (TotalCharges -> numeric, blanks -> NULL)
schemas.olap: Materialised views / aggregates for fast OLAP
schemas.ml: Feature tables, predictions, model run metadata
schemas.meta: Data dictionary, lineage, data-quality results (owned by metadata-api)

star_schema.grain: One row per customer subscription snapshot per load date

dimensions.dim_customer: customer_key (surrogate PK), customer_id (natural key), gender, senior_citizen, partner, dependents, valid_from, valid_to, is_current (SCD Type 2)
dimensions.dim_service: service_key, phone_service, multiple_lines, internet_service, online_security, online_backup, device_protection, tech_support, streaming_tv, streaming_movies
dimensions.dim_date: date_key (YYYYMMDD), date, day, week, month, month_name, quarter, year, is_weekend

star_schema.fact_customer_churn: customer_key, contract_key, service_key, payment_key, churn_key, date_key, tenure_band_key, tenure_months, monthly_charges, total_charges, churn_probability NULL, customer_count (=1)
constraints: Foreign keys from fact to every dimension
Indexes on every fact foreign key

olap_layer.approach: PostgreSQL GROUPING SETS / ROLLUP / CUBE plus materialised views refreshed CONCURRENTLY by Airflow after dbt runs
materialised_views: mv_churn_cube (CUBE over contract_type, payment_method, internet_service, tenure_band)

operations_to_support.roll_up: e.g. tenure_band -> all customers; month -> quarter -> year
operations_to_support.slice: fix one dimension value, e.g. contract_type = 'Month-to-month'
operations_to_support.dice: filter on several dimensions, e.g. contract in (...) and payment_method in (...)
operations_to_support.pivot: swap rows/columns of the result grid in the UI

airflow.executor: LocalExecutor for dev, CeleryExecutor (Valkey broker) for prod profile

steps: incremental extract from MySQL by updated_at watermark
dbt build (run + test) via BashOperator or Cosmos
publish data-quality results to meta schema
promote best model if it beats current champion on chosen metric
write ml.predictions and update fact churn_probability

requirements: SLA/failure alerts via email or webhook
connections and secrets via environment variables, never hard-coded

tests: unique + not_null on every surrogate key
relationships from fact to all dimensions
accepted_values for contract_type, payment_method, internet_service, churn_flag
custom test: fact row count equals distinct current customers
dbt.docs: dbt docs generate; expose manifest.json to metadata-api for lineage

topics.name: ingest.dlq.v1
topics.purpose: rejected or unprocessable records with error metadata

messaging_kafka.message_envelope: { event_id (UUID), event_type, schema_version, batch_id, produced_at, source, payload }
messaging_kafka.delivery: Producer acks=all, enable.idempotence=true; consumer at-least-once with idempotent upsert on event_id
messaging_kafka.schemas: JSON Schema files in contracts/ shared by producer, consumer and frontend

indexeddb_stores.metadata: data dictionary, dimension member lists, dropdown values (cached for offline forms)
indexeddb_stores.outbox: queued batches: { batch_id, idempotency_key, records[], checksum, status (PENDING|SENDING|ACCEPTED|PARTIAL|REJECTED), attempts, last_error, created_at }
indexeddb_stores.analytics_cache: last OLAP results and KPIs with fetched_at timestamp

behaviour: Validate each record in the browser with the same JSON Schema used by the server before queuing
Group records into batches of at most 500 records
Compute SHA-256 checksum of the batch payload
Sync on 'online' event, on app start and via Background Sync API where supported; manual 'Sync now' button otherwise
Exponential backoff with jitter on failure; max 8 attempts then mark FAILED for user review
Show per-row server errors and allow correction and resubmission
Show a clear online/offline indicator and pending-outbox count

validation_pipeline: reject duplicate Idempotency-Key by returning the original result
max payload size 5 MB and 500 records
business rules (tenure >= 0, monthly_charges > 0, total_charges >= monthly_charges when tenure > 0, enums valid)
server_side.response: { batch_id, status, accepted_count, rejected_count, errors: [{ row, field, code, message }], conflicts: [{ customer_id, server_version, client_version }] }
server_side.conflict_policy: Server wins by default; conflicts are returned to the client to resolve manually

roles.admin: manage users, metadata, pipelines and models
roles.data_steward: manage metadata and data dictionary, review rejected batches
roles.data_entry: create/update operational records and submit batches

api_gateway_and_auth.frontend_auth: Authorization Code flow with PKCE against Keycloak; tokens kept in memory, refresh token handled securely; offline mode allows viewing cached data and queuing writes, with the token refreshed before sync
api_gateway_and_auth.fine_grained_authorisation: Validate JWT again in FastAPI (defence in depth) and enforce role checks with dependency-injected guards

analytics_api: POST /api/v1/analytics/olap/query  body: { measures[], rows[], columns[], filters{}, operation: 'rollup'|'drilldown'|'slice'|'dice'|'pivot', limit }
rules: Whitelist dimensions and measures in the OLAP endpoint and build SQL with bound parameters only (no string-concatenated SQL)
Health endpoints /healthz and /readyz on every service

machine_learning.features: tenure, MonthlyCharges, TotalCharges and categorical customer, service, contract and payment attributes; exclude customerID
machine_learning.preprocessing: sklearn ColumnTransformer inside a Pipeline: numeric -> median imputation + StandardScaler; categorical -> most-frequent imputation + OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown='ignore'); fitted only on training folds to avoid leakage

evaluation.split: 80/20 stratified hold-out, random_state=42, plus stratified 5-fold cross-validation on the training set
extras: decision-threshold tuning on a validation fold
evaluation.champion_selection: Configurable metric (default: F1 on the churn class, since missed churners are costly); must also exceed ROC-AUC 0.83

machine_learning.registry_and_serving: MLflow tracking + model registry (aliases 'champion' and 'challenger'); analytics-api loads the champion at start-up and on 'model.promoted' Kafka event
responsible_use: Report that feature importance shows model reliance, not causation
Monitor prediction drift (PSI on key features) and log it
Do not use protected attributes (gender, senior_citizen) for automated decisions; report fairness metrics by group

pwa_frontend.framework: Next.js App Router, TypeScript strict mode
pwa_requirements: Web App Manifest with icons and theme colours
Service worker via Serwist: precache app shell, NetworkFirst for API GET with fallback to IndexedDB cache, never cache POST
Installable on Android, iOS and desktop

security: TLS everywhere in production (NGINX or APISIX termination)
All secrets in .env files excluded from git, with .env.example provided; support Docker secrets
Least-privilege database users per service (read-only user for analytics-api)
Parameterised queries only; input validation on every endpoint
CORS restricted to the PWA origin
Audit logging of all data-entry changes
Personal data minimisation; document a privacy note for real (non-sample) data
observability: Structured JSON logs with request/trace IDs propagated from the gateway
Prometheus metrics from APISIX, FastAPI (prometheus-fastapi-instrumentator), Kafka exporter, PostgreSQL and MySQL exporters, Airflow statsd
Grafana dashboards: API latency/error rate, Kafka consumer lag, DAG success rate, data freshness, model metrics

testing.backend: pytest with unit tests and integration tests using Testcontainers (MySQL, PostgreSQL, Kafka); minimum 80% coverage for services
testing.dbt: dbt build with all schema and custom tests passing; row-count reconciliation against baseline_validation_counts
testing.ml: Tests for pipeline leakage (preprocessing fitted only in training), reproducibility with fixed seeds, metric thresholds
testing.frontend: Vitest + React Testing Library for components; Playwright end-to-end tests including offline mode (context.setOffline) -> queue -> reconnect -> sync -> verify in warehouse
testing.load: k6 script for analytics and ingestion endpoints
testing.ci: GitHub Actions: lint (ruff, mypy, eslint, prettier), tests, dbt compile, Docker image builds

acceptance_criteria: 'make up' starts the whole stack from a clean machine with only Docker installed
After the first pipeline run, warehouse counts match baseline_validation_counts and all dbt tests pass with 0 invalid dimension links

OLAP explorer reproduces: month-to-month churn 1,655 of 3,875 (42.71%); one-year 166 of 1,473 (11.27%); two-year 48 of 1,695 (2.83%); tenure 0-12 months 1,037 of 2,186 (47.44%); electronic check 1,071 of 2,365 (45.29%)

A user can go offline, enter records and upload a CSV, come back online and see them synced, validated and visible in the warehouse after the next DAG run, with no duplicates when the same batch is resent
Requests without a valid Keycloak token are rejected by APISIX with 401; role restrictions return 403
Champion model ROC-AUC >= 0.83 on the hold-out set, with metrics logged in MLflow
PWA is installable and passes Lighthouse PWA and accessibility >= 90
No dependency requires a commercial licence
